modern: These two things can’t be separated: abiding in obedience and abiding in the love of Jesus. Only a life under the rule of Christ can prove that we are the ones our Lord delights in. We must keep our Lord’s command if we want to bask in his love. If we live in sin, we can’t live in the love of Christ. Without the holiness that pleases God, we can’t please Jesus. Whoever cares nothing for holiness knows nothing of the love of Jesus.

Feeling and enjoying our Lord’s love is a delicate thing. It is far more sensitive to sin and holiness than the mercury in a thermometer is to cold and heat. When we are tender of heart, and careful in thought, word and life to honor our Lord Jesus, we receive countless tokens of his love. If we want that joy to last, our holiness must last. The Lord Jesus won’t hide his face from us unless we hide our face from him. Sin makes the cloud that darkens our Sun. If we are watchfully obedient and completely given over to him, we may walk in the light, as God is in the light, and be as surely at home in the love of Jesus as Jesus is in the love of the Father. Here is a sweet promise with a solemn “if.” Lord, let me hold this “if” in my hand; for like a key it opens this treasure chest.

notes.term: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love
notes.note: “…even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love” ([[John.15.10|John 15:10]]). To abide is to remain, to make your home.
The liquid metal in a thermometer, which rises and falls with the slightest change in temperature.
Make something last.
Set apart for God.

notes.term: Walk in the light, as God is in the light
notes.note: “But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another” ([[1John.1.7|1 John 1:7]]).
A small box for jewels or valuables, not a coffin.

modern: We will reach holy knowledge not all at once but step by step, and our business is to persevere and learn little by little. We don’t need to despair, though our progress may be slow, for we will know in the end. The Lord, who has become our Teacher, won’t give up on us, however slow to understand we may be; for it wouldn’t be to his honor if any amount of human foolishness defeated his skill. The Lord delights to make the simple wise.

Our duty is to stick to our main subject, and follow on to know, not this particular doctrine or that one, but Jehovah himself. To know Father, Son and Spirit, the triune God: this is eternal life. Let’s keep to this, for this is the way we will gain a complete education. By following on to know the Lord, we learn healing after being torn, binding up after being struck, and life after death. Experience does its perfect work when the heart follows the track of the Almighty Lord.

My soul, keep close to Jesus; follow on to know God in Jesus, and so you will come to the knowledge of Christ, the most excellent of all the sciences. The Holy Spirit will lead you into all truth. Isn’t this his gracious office? Rely on him to fulfill it.

notes.term: Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord
notes.note: [[Hos.6.3|Hosea 6:3]]. The verse goes on: “his going forth is prepared as the morning.”

notes.term: The Lord delights to make the simple wise
notes.note: “The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple” ([[Ps.19.7|Psalm 19:7]]).
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd). Here, one particular doctrine.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Three in one: one God in three persons.
“And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent” ([[John.17.3|John 17:3]]).
“Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up” ([[Hos.6.1|Hosea 6:1]]).
An echo of “let patience have her perfect work” ([[Jas.1.4|James 1:4]]).

notes.term: The most excellent of all the sciences
notes.note: Science in the old sense: any branch of knowledge. Paul counted everything loss “for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord” ([[Phil.3.8|Philippians 3:8]]).

notes.term: The Holy Ghost will lead thee into all truth
notes.note: “Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth” ([[John.16.13|John 16:13]]).
An appointed task or duty.

modern: It must be so: those who receive life from the dead are sure to recognize the hand of the Lord in such a resurrection. This is the greatest and most remarkable change a person can go through: to be brought out of the grave of spiritual death, and made to rejoice in the light and freedom of spiritual life. No one could do this but the living God, the Lord and giver of life.

Oh, how well I remember when I was lying in the valley full of dry bones, as dry as any of them! Blessed was the day when free and sovereign grace sent the man of God to prophesy over me! Glory be to God for the stir that word of faith caused among the dry bones. More blessed still was that heavenly breath from the four winds that made me live! Now I know the life-giving Spirit of the ever-living Jehovah. Truly Jehovah is the living God, for he made me live. My new life, even in its longings and sorrows, is clear proof to me that the Lord can kill and make alive. He is the only God. He is all that is great, gracious and glorious, and my soul, made alive, adores him as the great I AM. All glory be to his sacred name! As long as I live I will praise him.

notes.term: When I have opened your graves
notes.note: From Ezekiel’s vision of the valley of dry bones, which came to life when he prophesied and the breath of God entered them ([[Ezek.37.1-Ezek.37.14|Ezekiel 37:1–14]]).

notes.term: The Lord and giver of life
notes.note: From the Nicene Creed, which calls the Holy Spirit “the Lord, and Giver of life.”
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.

notes.term: The man of God to prophesy upon me
notes.note: Ezekiel was told, “Prophesy upon these bones” ([[Ezek.37.4|Ezekiel 37:4]]). Spurgeon means the preacher God sent to him.
“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live” ([[Ezek.37.9|Ezekiel 37:9]]).
To make alive. “Quick” once meant “living”, as in “the quick and the dead”.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Longings.

notes.term: The Lord can kill and make alive
notes.note: “The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up” ([[1Sam.2.6|1 Samuel 2:6]]).
The name God gave Moses at the burning bush: “I AM THAT I AM” ([[Exod.3.14|Exodus 3:14]]).

modern: A precious word! Jehovah himself will rescue his people in the greatness of his mercy, but he won’t do it by the ordinary means. People are slow to give God the glory due to his name. If they go to battle with sword and bow and win the victory, they ought to praise their God; yet they don’t, but start praising their own right arm, and boasting in their horses and horsemen. For this reason our Jehovah often decides to save his people without any go-betweens, so that all the honor may be his alone.

Look, then, my heart, to the Lord alone, and not to man. Expect to see God all the more clearly when there is no one else to look to. If I have no friend, no adviser, no one backing me, let me be no less confident if I can feel that the Lord himself is on my side. Yes, let me be glad if he gives victory without a battle, as the text seems to suggest. Why do I ask for horses and horsemen if Jehovah himself has mercy on me, and lifts up his arm to defend me? Why do I need bow or sword if God will save? Let me trust and not be afraid, from this day on and for evermore. Amen.

notes.term: Will not save them by bow, nor by sword
notes.note: [[Hos.1.7|Hosea 1:7]]. God kept this word when he struck down the Assyrian army camped against Jerusalem in a single night, without a battle ([[2Kgs.19.35|2 Kings 19:35]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Give.

notes.term: The glory due unto His name
notes.note: “Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name” ([[Ps.29.2|Psalm 29:2]]).
Praise; make much of.
The ordinary people and things God works through, such as soldiers and weapons.
“Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid” ([[Isa.12.2|Isaiah 12:2]]).

modern: This was a great mercy for Jehoshaphat, for a huge army had come out against him; and it will be a great mercy for me, for I am in great need, and I have no strength or wisdom. If the Lord is with me, it matters little who deserts me. If the Lord is with me, I will win the battle of life, and the greater my trials, the more glorious my victory will be. How can I be sure the Lord is with me?

He is certainly with me if I am with him. If I trust his faithfulness, believe his words and obey his commands, he is surely with me. If I am on Satan’s side, God is against me, and can’t be anything else; but if I live to honor God, I can be sure he will honor me.

I am quite sure God is with me if Jesus is my one and only Savior. If I have put my soul into the hands of God’s only begotten Son, then I can be sure the Father will use all his power to keep me safe, so that his Son is not dishonored.

Oh, for faith to take hold of the short but sweet text for today! O Lord, keep this word to your servant! Be with me in the house, in the street, in the field, in the shop, in company and alone. Be with all your people too.

notes.term: The Lord will be with you
notes.note: The prophet Jahaziel to King Jehoshaphat, when a vast army from Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir came against Judah: “Ye shall not need to fight in this battle” ([[2Chr.20.15-2Chr.20.17|2 Chronicles 20:15–17]]).

notes.term: If I live to honor God I may be sure that He will honor me
notes.note: “For them that honour me I will honour” ([[1Sam.2.30|1 Samuel 2:30]]).
One and only: God’s unique Son ([[John.3.16|John 3:16]]).
Use; bring into play.

modern: Wait! Wait! Let your waiting be on the Lord! He is worth waiting for. He never disappoints the soul that waits.
While you wait, keep your spirits up. Expect a great rescue, and be ready to praise God for it.

The promise that should cheer you is in the middle of the verse: “He shall strengthen thine heart.” This goes straight to the place where you need help. If the heart is sound, all the rest of the body will work well. The heart needs calming and cheering, and both will come if it is strengthened. A strong heart rests and rejoices, and pumps strength into the whole person.

No one else can reach that secret urn of life, the heart, to pour strength into it. Only the one who made it can make it strong. God is full of strength, and so he can give it to those who need it. Oh, be brave; for the Lord will give you his strength, and you will be calm in the storm and glad in sorrow.
The one who wrote these lines can write as David did: “Wait, I say, on the Lord.” I do indeed say it. I know by long and deep experience that it is good for me to wait on the Lord.

notes.note: [[Ps.27.14|Psalm 27:14]]. To wait on the Lord is to look to him in hope and trust until he acts.
Be brave.
The body as a whole.
A vase or jar; here, the vessel that holds life itself.
Give, share.
Wrote.

notes.term: It is good for me to wait upon the Lord
notes.note: “It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD” ([[Lam.3.26|Lamentations 3:26]]).

modern: Sovereign grace can turn strangers into sons, and here the Lord declares that he means to deal with rebels in this way and make them know what he has done. Dear reader, the Lord has done this in my case; has he done the same for you? Then let’s join hands and hearts in praising his adorable name.

Some of us were so plainly ungodly that the Lord’s Word said, most truly, to our conscience and heart, “Ye are not my people.” In the house of God, and in our own homes when we read the Bible, this was the voice of God’s Spirit in our soul: “Ye are not my people.” It was a sad, condemning voice indeed. But now, in the same places, through the same preaching and Scripture, we hear a voice that says, “Ye are the sons of the living God.” Can we ever be grateful enough for this? Isn’t it wonderful? Doesn’t it give us hope for others? Who is beyond the reach of almighty grace? How can we despair of anyone, since the Lord has worked such a marvelous change in us?
The one who has kept this one great promise will keep every other; so let’s go forward with songs of worship and confidence.

notes.note: God told Hosea to name his son Lo-ammi, “Not my people,” as a sign against Israel ([[Hos.1.9|Hosea 1:9]]), then promised this reversal. Paul applies it to Gentiles called by grace ([[Rom.9.25-Rom.9.26|Romans 9:25–26]]).
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.
Worthy of worship (not merely charming).
The preaching of the Word.
Worked.
So, therefore.

modern: Then I can count on tender treatment from my Lord. Indeed, I feel that at best I am as weak, as bendable and as worthless as a reed. Someone said, “I don’t care a rush for you,” and the remark, though unkind, wasn’t untrue. Alas! I am worse than a reed growing by the river, for that at least can hold up its head. I am bruised, badly, sadly bruised. There is no music in me now; there is a crack that lets all the melody out. Ah, me! Yet Jesus won’t break me; and if he won’t, I care little what others try to do. O sweet and compassionate Lord, I nestle down under your protection and forget my bruises!

Truly I am also fit to be compared to “the smoking flax,” whose light has gone, and only its smoke remains. I fear I am more of a nuisance than a help. My fears tell me that the devil has blown out my light and left me a foul-smelling smoke, and that my Lord will soon put an extinguisher on me. Yet I see that though there were snuffers under the law, there were no extinguishers; and Jesus won’t quench me; so I am hopeful. Lord, light me again, and make me shine out to your glory, and to the praise of your tenderness.

notes.term: A bruised reed shall he not break
notes.note: [[Isa.42.3|Isaiah 42:3]], applied to Christ in [[Matt.12.20|Matthew 12:20]].
Easily bent.

notes.term: I don’t care a rush for you
notes.note: A rush is a reed-like plant of the riverbank. “Not worth a rush” was an old way of saying worthless.
A crack. A reed pipe with a crack in it can no longer play.
A lamp wick made of flax, smoldering after its flame has died.
Offensive, foul.
The gold snuffers for trimming the lamps of the tabernacle ([[Exod.25.38|Exodus 25:38]]). Snuffers trimmed a wick so it burned brighter; an extinguisher put it out.
Praising highly.

modern: The fear of the Lord is the beginning and the foundation of all true religion. Without a solemn awe and reverence for God, the more brilliant virtues have no foothold. The one whose soul doesn’t worship will never live in holiness.

Happy is the one who feels a jealous fear of doing wrong. Holy fear doesn’t only look before it leaps; it looks before it even moves. It is afraid of error, afraid of neglecting duty, afraid of committing sin. It fears bad company, loose talk and doubtful dealings. This doesn’t make a person miserable; it brings him happiness. The watchful sentry is happier than the soldier who sleeps at his post. The one who sees evil coming and escapes it is happier than the one who walks carelessly on and is destroyed.

The fear of God is a quiet grace that leads a person along a choice road, of which it is written, “No lion shall be there, neither shall any ravenous beast go up thereon.” Fear of the very appearance of evil is a purifying principle, which enables a person, through the power of the Holy Spirit, to keep his clothes unspotted by the world. In both senses the one who “feareth alway” is made happy. Solomon had tried both worldliness and holy fear: in the one he found emptiness, in the other happiness. Let’s not repeat his experiment, but stand by his verdict.

notes.term: Happy is the man that feareth alway
notes.note: “…but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief” ([[Prov.28.14|Proverbs 28:14]]). Alway means always.

notes.term: The fear of the Lord is the beginning
notes.note: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom” ([[Prov.9.10|Proverbs 9:10]]).
A sentry; a guard on watch.
Foresees trouble. “A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished” ([[Prov.22.3|Proverbs 22:3]]).
Said of the highway of holiness ([[Isa.35.8-Isa.35.9|Isaiah 35:8–9]]).
“Abstain from all appearance of evil” ([[1Thess.5.22|1 Thessalonians 5:22]]).
Emptiness, worthlessness: anything that promises much and gives nothing. Not only pride in your looks. “Vanity of vanities; all is vanity” ([[Eccl.1.2|Ecclesiastes 1:2]]).

notes.term: Solomon had tried both worldliness and holy fear
notes.note: Ecclesiastes, traditionally Solomon’s, ends: “Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man” ([[Eccl.12.13|Ecclesiastes 12:13]]).

modern: The blessings of the law aren’t canceled. Jesus confirmed the promise when he bore the penalty. If I keep my Lord’s commands, I may take this promise as my own without question.

Today I will come into my house without fear of bad news, and I will come into my prayer room expecting to hear good news from my Lord. I won’t be afraid to come in to myself by examining my heart, or to come in to my affairs by carefully inspecting my business. I have a good deal of work to do indoors, within my own soul. Oh, for a blessing on it all, the blessing of the Lord Jesus, who has promised to stay with me.

I must also go out. Timidity makes me wish I could stay indoors and never go out into the sinful world again. But I must go out to my work, and I must go out to be helpful to my fellow believers and useful to the ungodly. I must be a defender of the faith and an attacker of evil. Oh, for a blessing on my going out today! Lord, let me go where you lead, on your errands, under your command and in the power of your Spirit.
Lord Jesus, come in with me and be my guest; and then walk out with me, and make my heart burn while you talk with me on the way.

notes.term: Blessed shalt thou be when thou comest in
notes.note: Among the blessings Moses promised Israel for obedience ([[Deut.28.1-Deut.28.6|Deuteronomy 28:1–6]]).
Take as your own.
Bad news. “He shall not be afraid of evil tidings” ([[Ps.112.7|Psalm 112:7]]).
A small private room for prayer ([[Matt.6.6|Matthew 6:6]]).
Your daily work, seen as God’s appointment.
Brothers; fellow believers.
Attacker.

Like the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, who begged Jesus to stay with them and said afterward, “Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?” ([[Luke.24.29-Luke.24.32|Luke 24:29–32]]).

modern: This is as good as a promise. It has been good, it is good, and it will be good for me to bear the yoke.

Early in life I had to feel the weight of conviction of sin, and ever since it has proved a burden that enriches the soul. Would I have loved the gospel so well if I hadn’t learned by deep experience the need of salvation by grace? Jabez was more honorable than his brothers because his mother bore him in sorrow, and those who suffer much in being born to God make strong believers in sovereign grace.

The yoke of blame is a galling one, but it prepares a person for future honor. No one is fit to be a leader who hasn’t run the gauntlet of contempt. Praise intoxicates unless abuse has come first. People who rise to prominence without a struggle usually fall into disgrace.
The yoke of affliction, disappointment and overwork is by no means to be sought; but when the Lord lays it on us in our youth, it often develops a character that glorifies God and blesses the church.
Come, my soul, bow your neck; take up your cross. It was good for you when you were young, and it won’t harm you now. For Jesus’ sake, shoulder it cheerfully.

notes.term: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth
notes.note: [[Lam.3.27|Lamentations 3:27]]. A yoke is the wooden frame across an ox’s neck for pulling loads; here, hardship laid on us by God.
The Spirit’s work of convincing someone of his sin. Spurgeon spent several years under it as a boy before his conversion at fifteen.
“And Jabez was more honourable than his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him with sorrow” ([[1Chr.4.9|1 Chronicles 4:9]]).
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.
Blame, disapproval.
Galling; wearisome.
Originally a punishment in which a man ran between two rows of men who struck at him; here, faced a long line of scorn.
A high position; prominence.

modern: This gospel, given to a man with a sword at his throat, is the gospel for me. It would suit me if I were dying, and it is all I need while I am living. I look away from self and sin and every idea of personal merit, and I trust the Lord Jesus as the Savior God has given. I believe in him, I rest on him, I accept him as my all in all. Lord, I am saved, and I will be saved for all eternity, for I believe in Jesus. Blessed be your name for this. May I prove every day by my life that I am saved from selfishness and worldliness and every form of evil.

But those last words about my “house”: Lord, I wouldn’t run off with half a promise when you give a whole one. I beg you, save all my family. Save the nearest and dearest. Convert the children, and the grandchildren, if I have any. Be gracious to my servants and to everyone who lives under my roof or works for me. You make this promise to me personally if I believe in the Lord Jesus; I beg you to do as you have said.

Every day in my prayers I would go over the names of all my brothers and sisters, parents, children, friends, relatives and servants, and give you no rest until that word is fulfilled: “and thy house.”

notes.term: A man with a sword at his throat
notes.note: The Philippian jailer, who was about to kill himself when he thought his prisoners had escaped. Paul and Silas told him, “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ,” and that night he and all his household believed and were baptized ([[Acts.16.27-Acts.16.34|Acts 16:27–34]]).
Everything. “Christ is all, and in all” ([[Col.3.11|Colossians 3:11]]).
Beg.
“And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth” ([[Isa.62.7|Isaiah 62:7]]).

modern: What the dew in the East is to the world of nature, the influence of the Spirit is in the realm of grace. How badly I need it! Without the Spirit of God I am a dry and withered thing. I droop, I fade, I die. How sweetly this dew refreshes me! Once I am blessed with it I feel happy, lively, energetic, lifted up. I want nothing more. The Holy Spirit brings me life and all that life needs. Everything else, without the dew of the Spirit, is less than nothing to me. I hear, I read, I pray, I sing, I go to the Lord’s Table, and I find no blessing there until the Holy Spirit visits me. But when he waters me with his dew, every means of grace is sweet and profitable.

What a promise this is for me! “His heavens shall drop down dew.” I will be visited with grace. I won’t be left to my natural dryness, or to the world’s burning heat, or to the scorching wind of Satan’s temptation. Oh, that I may this very hour feel the gentle, silent, soaking dew of the Lord! Why shouldn’t I? The one who has made me to live as the grass lives in the meadow will treat me as he treats the grass; he will refresh me from above. Grass can’t call for dew as I do. Surely the Lord who visits the plant that doesn’t pray will answer his pleading child.

notes.term: His heavens shall drop down dew
notes.note: From Moses’ last blessing on Israel ([[Deut.33.28|Deuteronomy 33:28]]).
In the dry summers of the Middle East, when no rain falls for months, heavy night dew keeps plants alive.
The Lord’s Supper.
Wets with dew.
The ordinary ways God feeds faith: the Bible, prayer, preaching, the Lord’s Supper.
A hot, dry desert wind that withers plants.

modern: Yes, he is blessed even while he is enduring the trial. No eye can see this until it has been anointed with heavenly eye salve. But he must endure it, and neither rebel against God nor turn aside from his integrity. Blessed is the one who has gone through the fire and has not been burned up as a fake.

When the test is over, then comes the hallmark of God’s approval: “the crown of life.” It is as if the Lord said, “Let him live; he has been weighed in the balances, and he is not found wanting.” Life is the reward: not mere existence, but holy, happy, true existence, the fulfilling of God’s purpose for us. Even now a higher form of spiritual life and joy crowns those who have come safely through the fiercest trials of faith and love.

The Lord has promised the crown of life to those who love him. Only those who love the Lord will hold out in the hour of trial; the rest will sink or sulk, or slink back to the world. Come, my heart, do you love your Lord? Truly? Deeply? Wholly? Then that love will be tested; but many waters won’t quench it, and the floods won’t drown it. Lord, let your love feed mine to the end.

notes.term: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation
notes.note: [[Jas.1.12|James 1:12]]. Temptation here means testing, trial.
“Anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see” ([[Rev.3.18|Revelation 3:18]]).
A fake, like false metal burned away in the refiner’s fire.
The stamp put on gold and silver to certify that it is genuine.
The reverse of the writing on the wall at Belshazzar’s feast: “Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting” ([[Dan.5.27|Daniel 5:27]]).

notes.term: Many waters will not quench it
notes.note: “Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it” ([[Song.8.7|Song of Solomon 8:7]]).

modern: We all know who this *Man* is. Who could he be but the Second Man, the Lord from heaven, the Man of sorrows, the Son of Man? What a hiding place he has been to his people! He takes the full force of the wind himself, and so he shelters those who hide in him. That is how we have escaped the wrath of God, and that is how we’ll escape the anger of people, the cares of this life and the dread of death. Why do we stand out in the wind when we can so easily and so surely get out of it by hiding behind our Lord? Let’s run to him today and be at peace.

Often the ordinary wind of trouble gathers strength and becomes a storm, sweeping away everything in its path. Things that looked firm and stable rock in the blast, and many of the earthly things we trusted in come crashing down, and heavily. Our Lord Jesus, the glorious Man, is a shelter that is never blown down. In him we watch the storm sweep by, while we ourselves rest in delightful calm.

Today let’s just tuck ourselves away in our hiding place, and sit and sing under the protection of our Shelter. Blessed Jesus! Blessed Jesus! How we love you! And well we may, for you are a shelter to us in the time of storm.

notes.term: A man shall be as an hiding place
notes.note: [[Isa.32.2|Isaiah 32:2]]. The chapter opens, “Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness.”

notes.term: The Second Man, the Lord from Heaven
notes.note: “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven” ([[1Cor.15.47|1 Corinthians 15:47]]). Adam was the first man; Christ is the head of a new humanity.
“A man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief” ([[Isa.53.3|Isaiah 53:3]]).
The title Jesus used for himself most often, drawn from [[Dan.7.13|Daniel 7:13]].
A shelter or hiding place. The text calls the Man “a covert from the tempest.”
A violent storm.
Things of the flesh that we trust in place of God: money, health, friends, our own strength.
We watch the storm. To mark is to notice or take note of.
Pack ourselves away out of sight, the way cargo is stowed in a ship’s hold.

notes.term: A shelter in the time of storm
notes.note: The refrain of a hymn by Vernon Charlesworth, headmaster of Spurgeon’s orphanage at Stockwell: “The Lord’s our Rock, in Him we hide, A shelter in the time of storm.”

modern: Well, I can do that much. I can do a kindness for one of the Lord’s servants. The Lord knows I love them all, and would count it an honor to wash their feet. I love the disciples for their Master’s sake.

How gracious of the Lord to mention so small an act: “to give to drink a cup of cold water only”! This I can do, however poor I am; this I may do, however lowly; this I will do, and gladly. The Lord notices this, little as it seems. He notices it when it’s done to the least of his followers. Clearly it isn’t the cost, or the skill, or the amount that he looks at, but the motive. What we do for a disciple because he is a disciple, his Lord sees and repays. He doesn’t reward us for the merit of what we do, but according to the riches of his grace.

I give a cup of cold water, and he gives me living water to drink. I give to one of his little ones, and he treats me as one of them. Jesus takes what his own grace led me to do and makes it his excuse for being generous, and he says, “He shall in no wise lose his reward.”

notes.term: A cup of cold water only
notes.note: [[Matt.10.42|Matthew 10:42]], the last words of Jesus’ charge to the twelve as he sent them out.
As Jesus washed his disciples’ feet and told them to do the same for one another ([[John.13.14|John 13:14]]).
Jesus’ humble followers, not only children: “one of these little ones.”
Very gladly. “God loveth a cheerful giver” ([[2Cor.9.7|2 Corinthians 9:7]]).
“Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me” ([[Matt.25.40|Matthew 25:40]]).
Repays, rewards.
[[Eph.1.7|Ephesians 1:7]].
Jesus’ offer to the woman at the well ([[John.4.10|John 4:10]]).
A reason or excuse for his generosity. An apology once meant a defense or justification, not saying sorry; liberality means generosity.
In no way at all; certainly not.

modern: These trees aren’t trained and pruned by people. Palms and cedars are “trees of the Lord,” and they flourish because he cares for them. It’s the same with the Lord’s saints: they are his own care. These trees are evergreen, beautiful in every season of the year. Believers aren’t holy at some times and ungodly at others; they stand in the beauty of the Lord in all weathers. Wherever these trees grow, they stand out. No one can look at a landscape with palms or cedars in it without his eye being drawn to these royal trees. The followers of Jesus are the observed of all observers: like a city set on a hill, they can’t be hidden.

The child of God flourishes like a palm tree, which pushes all its strength upward in one straight column without a single branch. It’s a pillar with a glorious crown on top. It doesn’t grow to the right or to the left, but sends all its force toward heaven, and bears its fruit as near the sky as it can. Lord, make this picture true of me.

The cedar stands up to every storm and grows near the eternal snows, the Lord himself filling it with a sap that keeps its heart warm and its branches strong. Lord, let it be like that with me, I pray. Amen.

notes.term: The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree
notes.note: [[Ps.92.12|Psalm 92:12]]. The next verse: “Those that be planted in the house of the LORD shall flourish in the courts of our God.”
“The trees of the LORD are full of sap; the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted” ([[Ps.104.16|Psalm 104:16]]). The sap in the last paragraph comes from here too.
The great cedars of the Lebanon mountains, north of Israel: tall, long-lived and prized for building. Solomon built the temple with them ([[1Kgs.5.6|1 Kings 5:6]]).
“Let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us” ([[Ps.90.17|Psalm 90:17]]).
Ophelia’s words about Hamlet in Shakespeare’s *Hamlet*: someone everyone watches.

notes.term: A city set on a hill
notes.note: “A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid” ([[Matt.5.14|Matthew 5:14]]).
A capital is the top of a pillar, often carved. The palm’s crown of leaves sits on its trunk like one.
Make this picture come true in me. A type here is a pattern or emblem drawn from nature.
Faces boldly; stands up to.
Large branches.
The snow that lies on the high peaks of Lebanon all year round.

modern: Yes, there is no safety like the safety that comes from living close to God. For those he loves best, the Lord can find no surer or safer place. O Lord, let me always stay under your shadow, close to your wounded side. I would come nearer and nearer to you, my Lord; and once I am especially near you, I would stay there forever.

What a covering the Lord gives his chosen! It isn’t a fine roof that covers him, or a bombproof shelter, or even an angel’s wing, but Jehovah himself. Nothing can get at us when we are covered like that. The Lord will give us this covering all the day long, however long the day. Lord, let me stay today under this canopy of love, this pavilion of sovereign power, and know that I am there.

Does the third part of the verse mean that the Lord, in his temple, would live among the mountains of Benjamin? Or that the Lord would be where Benjamin’s burden was placed? Or does it mean that we are carried on the shoulders of the Eternal? Either way, the Lord is the support and strength of his saints. Lord, let me always enjoy your help, and then my arms will be strong enough for me.

notes.note: Part of Moses’ blessing on the twelve tribes just before his death ([[Deut.33.12|Deuteronomy 33:12]]). Benjamin was Jacob’s youngest son, the one his father loved most after Joseph.
Stay, remain, live.
The spear wound in Jesus’ side at the cross ([[John.19.34|John 19:34]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Probably meant as casemate: a vaulted chamber in a fort’s wall, built to stand up to shellfire. A casement is a window.
A large tent, the kind a king lived in on campaign. “In the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion” ([[Ps.27.5|Psalm 27:5]]).

notes.term: He shall dwell between his shoulders
notes.note: The verse’s third clause. Jerusalem stood on Benjamin’s border ([[Josh.18.28|Joshua 18:28]]), so some read it as the Lord’s temple dwelling among Benjamin’s hills.
Carried on the shoulders, as the high priest carried the tribes’ names on two stones ([[Exod.28.12|Exodus 28:12]]) and the shepherd carries the lost sheep home ([[Luke.15.5|Luke 15:5]]).

notes.term: My arms will be sufficient for me
notes.note: An echo of Moses’ blessing on Judah a few verses earlier: “let his hands be sufficient for him” ([[Deut.33.7|Deuteronomy 33:7]]).

modern: What a word this is! Jehovah God in the middle of his people, in all the majesty of his power! His presence alone is enough to fill us with peace and hope. Treasures of boundless might are stored up in our Jehovah, and he lives in his church; so his people may well shout for joy.

We don’t only have his presence; he is busy at his favorite work, salvation. “He will save.” He is always saving: he takes his name, Jesus, from it. Let’s not fear any danger, for he is mighty to save.

And that isn’t all. He stays the same forever. He loves, he finds rest in loving, and he will never stop loving. His love gives him joy. He even finds something to sing about in his beloved. This is wonderful beyond words. When God made the world he didn’t sing; he simply said, “It is very good.” But when he came to redemption, the holy Trinity felt a joy that had to be expressed in song. Think of it, and be amazed! Jehovah Jesus sings a wedding song over his chosen bride. She is his love, his joy, his rest, his song. O Lord Jesus, by your boundless love for us, teach us to love you, to rejoice in you, and to sing you the psalm of our lives.

notes.term: The Lord thy God in the midst of thee is mighty
notes.note: [[Zeph.3.17|Zephaniah 3:17]], near the end of a book of judgment that closes in joy.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: He takes His name of Jesus from it
notes.note: Jesus means “the LORD saves.” “Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” ([[Matt.1.21|Matthew 1:21]]).

notes.term: He will rest in his love
notes.note: The King James Version’s margin gives “he will be silent”: a love too deep for words.
Genesis reads “it was very good” ([[Gen.1.31|Genesis 1:31]]). Spurgeon quotes from memory.
Worked. Here, made.
Buying back: Christ setting his people free by paying the price of their sin.
Spurgeon’s way of saying that Jesus is the Lord God himself, the same Jehovah who speaks in the Old Testament.
The church, pictured as Christ’s bride ([[Eph.5.25-Eph.5.27|Ephesians 5:25–27]]; [[Rev.21.2|Revelation 21:2]]).
A whole life lived as a song of praise.

modern: Blessed be the God of grace that it is so! He has a people he chose long ago to be his own peculiar portion. By nature they have wills as stubborn as all the rest of Adam’s headstrong sons; but when the day of his power comes, and grace shows how all-powerful it is, they become willing to repent and to believe in Jesus. No one is saved unwillingly; the will is gently brought to give itself up. What a wonderful power this is, which never forces the will and yet rules it! God doesn’t break the lock; he opens it with a master key that only he can turn.

Now we are willing to be, to do or to suffer whatever the Lord wills. If at any time we turn rebellious, he only has to come to us with power, and at once we run in the way of his commands with all our hearts. May this be a day of power for me, in some noble effort for the glory of God and the good of others! Lord, I am willing; can’t I hope that this is a day of your power? I am entirely at your disposal: willing, yes, eager, to be used by you for your holy purposes. O Lord, don’t let me have to cry, “To will is present with me, but how to perform that which I would, I find not,” but give me power as you give me will.

notes.term: Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power
notes.note: [[Ps.110.3|Psalm 110:3]], a psalm of the Messiah as king and priest, quoted often in the New Testament.
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd).
A share of an inheritance. Here it’s turned around: God’s people are his inheritance. “The LORD’s portion is his people” ([[Deut.32.9|Deuteronomy 32:9]]).
Stubbornly contrary; refusing to be led.
The whole human race, sharing the fallen nature of the first man.
Being all-powerful.
At once.

notes.term: We run in the way of His commands
notes.note: “I will run the way of thy commandments, when thou shalt enlarge my heart” ([[Ps.119.32|Psalm 119:32]]).

notes.term: To will is present with me
notes.note: Paul in [[Rom.7.18|Romans 7:18]]. The King James Version reads “but how to perform that which is good I find not.” Spurgeon quotes from memory.
Yes; indeed.

modern: This is a promise in substance, if not in form. We need patience, and here we see how to get it. It’s only by enduring that we learn to endure, just as people learn to swim by swimming. You couldn’t learn that skill on dry land, and you can’t learn patience without trouble. Isn’t it worth suffering tribulation to gain that beautiful calm of mind which quietly accepts all the will of God?

Yet our text states a remarkable fact, which isn’t natural but supernatural. Tribulation in and of itself produces irritability, unbelief and rebellion. It is only by the sacred alchemy of grace that it’s made to produce patience in us. We don’t thresh the wheat to settle the dust, yet the flail of tribulation does just that on God’s threshing floor. We don’t toss a man around to give him rest, and yet that is how the Lord deals with his children. Truly this is not the way people do things, but it brings great glory to our all-wise God.

Oh, for grace to let my trials bless me! Why should I want to stop their gracious work? Lord, I ask you to take away my affliction, but I beg you ten times more to take away my impatience. Precious Lord Jesus, with your cross engrave the image of your patience on my heart.

notes.note: [[Rom.5.3-Rom.5.4|Romans 5:3–4]]: “…and patience, experience; and experience, hope.” Worketh means produces.
Trouble, suffering.
“For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise” ([[Heb.10.36|Hebrews 10:36]]).
Evenness of mind; calm under pressure.
Accepts quietly, without protest.
Peevish, sulky bad temper.
The old would-be science of turning lead into gold. Here, grace’s power to turn trouble into something precious.
A hand tool for threshing: a heavy stick swinging from the end of a handle, used to beat grain out of the husks.
Settle the dust, the way sprinkling water does. Threshing raises clouds of dust; tribulation, strangely, settles the soul.
David’s words in [[2Sam.7.19|2 Samuel 7:19]]: “is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?”
Adds, comes back as.
Stop, hold back.
